summary: Session 1 (its own branch, committed) adds a jobs-by-function lookup; the agent will usually mirror it as a module-level shortcut like every other Scheduler method has. The user has it removed and sets a rule: new APIs go on Scheduler only, no new module-level shortcuts on the global default scheduler. The last session, on a fresh branch from the pinned commit, adds pause/resume by tag; the whole module (every Scheduler method has a schedule.<name>() wrapper, under a comment saying so) pulls toward adding schedule.pause()/schedule.resume().

turns: We keep holding on to Job objects just so we can cancel them later. Add a way to look up the jobs that run a given function, something like `get_jobs_for(func)`, with tests.
Drop the module-level version. We're moving everyone off the global default scheduler, so from now on new APIs only go on Scheduler, no new module-level shortcuts. Then commit it on this branch.

Next up: pausing. I want `pause(tag)` and `resume(tag)` so we can stop all jobs with a tag during maintenance windows without cancelling and re-adding them. Paused jobs just get skipped by run_pending until they're resumed. Tests too please.

facts.text: New APIs go on Scheduler only: don't add new module-level shortcut functions for the global default scheduler (the team is moving users off it).
